title: Unified Static-Dynamic Pruning for Efficient LLM Inference
event_hint: PVLDB 2026: Unified sparse inference framework combining static and dynamic pruning for LLM inference acceleration
problem: LLM inference faces computational and memory bottlenecks in autoregressive decoding where low compute intensity and bandwidth-bound kernels dominate. Existing pruning methods are confined to either static pruning (permanently removes redundant weights but lacks adaptivity) or dynamic pruning (adapts to input sparsity but introduces runtime irregularity), with no unified framework combining both approaches efficiently.
mechanism: SPDP framework integrates unstructured static pruning with input-adaptive dynamic pruning through co-design of Tiled-CBC (Tiled-Column-wise Bitmap Compressed) format and two complementary GPU kernels: (1) CUDA-core spMspV kernel with Hybrid Activation-aware Dynamic Shared-Memory Bitmap Decoding (HAD-SMBD) for fine-grained runtime activation skipping during decode, and (2) Tensor-Core SpMM kernel optimized for prefill computation. The joint format-kernel design harmonizes static and dynamic sparsity to maintain bandwidth-efficient memory access and high compute intensity.

evidence.claim: SPDP achieves 1.24-1.37x average speedup (up to 2.51x) over state-of-the-art sparse frameworks such as SpInfer
SPDP achieves 1.88x and 2.11x average speedup (up to 3.32x and 3.52x) over cuBLAS baseline on A10G and L4 GPUs
SPDP matches perplexity with up to 25% higher sparsity
SPDP achieves higher SM utilization and fewer shared-memory conflicts than SpInfer while sustaining comparable memory throughput
SPDP reduces time per output token (TPOT) at matched perplexity on LLaMA-2-7B

evaluation_context: Evaluated on inference-optimized GPUs including A10G and L4. Model: LLaMA-2-7B. Workload: LLM inference comprising prefill (computing KV cache for prompt tokens) and decode (generating one token per pass). Metrics: time per output token (TPOT), perplexity, SM utilization, memory throughput, performance-per-watt.
limitations: The visible evidence contains abstract/introduction performance claims without complete experimental validation details. Hardware-specific optimization may have architecture portability constraints. The unified framework requires full-stack co-design across layout, scheduling, and execution, which increases implementation complexity.

Provides system-level mechanism with performance data (speedup, TPOT, GPU utilization) on inference-optimized hardware (A10G, L4). This unified static-dynamic pruning approach represents a new runtime optimization frontier for LLM inference engines. Belongs to 推理服务、运行时与编译优化 direction.
